faqs.q: Sec. 98-93. - Violations; summons and complaint; civil recourse; penalty.
faqs.a:
(a)
It shall be a violation of this chapter to fail to perform any applicable affirmative
               duty specified in this chapter including, but not limited to the:
(1)
Failure of any person engaged in business in the city to obtain a license;
(2)
Failure of any taxpayer to file a timely return or to make timely payment of any total
               tax liability;
(3)
Failure of any resident individual or business to comply with the registration requirements
               for automotive vehicles;
(4)
Making of any false or fraudulent statement by any person in any return, claim for
               refund, or hearing; or
(5)
Evasion of collection of any tax by any person or the aiding or abetting of any other
               person in an attempt to evade the timely payment of tax due.
(b)
The finance director may direct the issuance of a complaint and summons to appear
               before the municipal court of the city to any person who may be in violation of this
               chapter or of the rules and regulations promulgated by the finance director.
(c)
Nothing in this chapter shall limit the ability of the city to collect taxes in a
               civil suit.
(d)
Violations of this chapter shall be punishable by a fine or imprisonment or both pursuant
               to the limits established in
section 1-5
. Each and every 24 hour continuation of any violation shall constitute a distinct
               and separate offense.
(Code 1981, § 31-63.2; Ord. No. 3783, § 2, 12-16-2002)
